findings.title: Leaving the beds becomes an embodied address
findings.claim: The preceding verse presents believers falling in prostration; here their sides separate from their resting places and their call to the Lord is held between fear and eager hope. The later hidden recompense and paired destinations make those two orientations consequential within the pericope, while the focus itself leaves their precise objects open.
findings.mechanism: The focus's separative movement joins the body's side to a concrete resting place, then gives that bodily departure a vocal direction through yadʿūna rabbahum. The paired khawfan and ṭamaʿan orient the call at once toward feared harm and hoped-for good. The supplied 32:15 connection places the act after prostration; 32:17 and 32:19–20 supply hidden recompense and contrasting outcomes that color the fear–hope pair without replacing the plain scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The verse's devotion becomes a bodily and vocal movement together: contact with rest is released, the Lord is addressed, and fear and hope sit amid stakes the surrounding passage makes visible.
findings.containment: The focus still says that sides move away from beds, that they call on their Lord in fear and hope, and that they spend from what was provided. It does not name the exact object of either feeling, and the later destinations do not prove a one-to-one mapping. The sequence does not establish one uninterrupted physical episode or a rejection of rest.

epistemic.reason: The focus wording and channel evidence are citable and the adjacent Arabic is supplied; assigning the fear and hope to particular later outcomes remains a contextual inference.

findings.containment: The focus still plainly says that they spend from what was provided. In the same pericope, 32:19 presents a receiving abode and hospitality, while 32:20 describes an adverse enclosure from which attempted exits lead back inside. The traced 32:19 abode and welcome provide a receiving destination; the 32:20 abode, attempted khurūj, and forced ʿawd provide a closed exit-return pattern. The n-f-q outlet branch meets that pattern analogically, changing two meritorious acts into present capacities for release before a future enclosure.

The HFT author's bed-as-micro-abode and present-actions-as-rehearsal are explicitly an inference; here they remain an analogy, not a literal equation or stated purpose. The supplied 32:20 connection calls the relation a broad contrast, and separate devotional acts followed by separate fates remains a live reading.
